jobs.title: Content Manager
jobs.description:

With 144 suites by Joseph Dirand and a collection of dynamic dining and bar spaces, it’s a place where experiences are curated, conversations flow, and every detail matters.

As Content Manager, you will lead the creation of premium photography and videography that brings The Chancery Rosewood’s products, people, and brand story to life — a rare opportunity to shape the visual identity of one of Mayfair’s most exciting new luxury hotels, reporting to the Digital and Social Manager.

**Key Responsibilities**

•
    
Lead photography and videography production end-to-end — from creative concept and shoot direction to editing and final delivery across every platform.

•
    
Direct talent, colleagues, and external creative partners during shoots, keeping every production calm, collaborative, and on schedule.

•
    
Develop and maintain a content calendar aligned with marketing campaigns and business objectives, capturing product, lifestyle, event, and branded content across the hotel.

•
    
Manage the hotel’s digital asset library, ensuring content is correctly labelled, accessible, and consistent in colour grading, sound quality, and visual identity.

•
    
Work closely with the Head of Digital to maximise engagement, reach, and brand consistency across all visual content.

Connection — You build strong relationships across Sales & Marketing, other departments, and external creative partners, bringing people with you through clear briefing and collaboration.

•

•
    
Drive — You approach every brief with creative ambition and personal accountability, continuously developing your knowledge of production techniques and platform trends.

•
    
Adaptability — You manage multiple shoots, edits, and deadlines with composure, responding constructively to last-minute changes without compromising on quality.

•
    
Initiative — You proactively plan shoots ahead of need, developing a content calendar that keeps the hotel’s storytelling one step ahead.

•
    
Strategic Thinking — You contribute creative insight that informs the hotel’s digital engagement strategy, staying ahead of platform guidelines and trends.

•
    
Business Acumen — You ensure every production is commercially focused and delivered on schedule, analysing content performance to prioritise the shoots that drive the greatest engagement.

•
    
People Leadership — You direct talent and external partners with clear guidance, fostering a collaborative culture and contributing to the professional development of colleagues involved in content creation.

12 complimentary room nights across The Rosewood Hotel portfolio (friends & family rates also available)

Flexible benefits app and monthly allowance to spend on whatever you like

Up to 16 weeks paid parental leave

Birthday day off - A paid day of leave for your birthday

Developmental & social calendars

Life insurance

Enhanced sick pay policy

jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
**About Kernel**
AI agents are starting to do sales, procurement and operations work. They need to know which company they are dealing with.
  
  
Most company data is in CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets. Records are duplicated, parent companies are missing, and addresses are outdated. This costs sales teams revenue and leaves operations and finance teams with avoidable risk and bad debt. Agents need a business identity layer they can trust.
  
  
Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. Every business gets a permanent KERN ID, along with the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at
**Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout**
already use Kernel in their own systems, and we expect agents to use it far more.
  
  
We have raised
**$20M**
from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing
**12x YoY**
.
  
  
**The role**
You’ll be
**Kernel’s Product Marketing Lead**
, building product marketing from the ground up. There’s a lot of potential here, and you’ll set the direction.
  
  
Your mission:
**make Kernel easy to understand and easy to buy**
, for customers and for the partners who sell it.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Own positioning and narrative: for customers we sell to directly and for our partners.
* Write the technical story: work with Anders, Marcus, and Zak on product positioning and technical documentation.
* Own announcements and launches: plan each one and get it out.
* Equip sales: work with the sales team on messaging, demos and battlecards.
* Build our social proof: case studies and customer references.
* 5% “other stuff”: events, the website and anything else that helps the business.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Most important is product marketing experience at a high-growth startup and examples of work that had a real impact on the business.
* You have written technical content before.
* You have led large projects such as a launch or a repositioning, and set the plan yourself.
* You work fast and closely with sales and the founders.
* You have taste and you execute well.
* Experience with video content is a plus but not a requirement.

**⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:**

* Need other product marketers around you to work best.
* Prefer to be handed a brief than to write one.
* Need perfect clarity before starting.
* Prefer long cycles and big “reveals.”
* Want fully remote work (we move faster in-person).

**What We Offer**
We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.
  
  

* 💰 Salary: £90,000 – £120,000 base + equity
* 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays
* 🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance
* ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere
* 🍼 Generous parental leave policy
* 💼 Pension plan
* 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office
* 🎉 Team events and dinners
* 🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI
* 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

**🎫 Visas & Relocation**
We sponsor visas for exceptional candidates and provide relocation support for those moving to London.
  
  
**Interview Process**
**Stage 1:**
Introductory Call with Zak, Founding Growth (30 minutes)
  
  
**Stage 2:**
Case Study with Zak & Anders (CEO)
  
  
**Final Stage:**
Founders Interview. A conversation with the founders focused on values alignment and long-term vision.
  
  
*Following Mutual Fit: Reference checks and offer stage.*

Togather are the team at the heart of great events.
  
  
We're a founder-led company of 40+ event specialists working across some of the largest and most exciting events in the UK.
  
  
Our Marketplace supports both B2B and B2C customers to handpick standout suppliers across street food, drink and venues for private events, from large-scale summer and Christmas parties to regular office lunches for clients including Spotify, Netflix & BBC.
  
  
Live partners with organisers of large-scale public events, using our 360 tech and industry expertise to curate and deliver exceptional food and drink experiences that also drive commercial results for our clients. From major festivals, stadium fanzones and cultural celebrations, we work hand in hand with client teams to deliver exceptional guest experience for the likes of GALA festival, Rock Oyster, Hill Dickinson Stadium and Pride in London.
  
  
Internally, we're proud to have been recognised by Tempo and the Startups 100 Awards as one of the UK's best places to work. We care deeply about building an ambitious, supportive and high-performing team.
  
  
We started life 10 years ago as Feast It, a two-person marketplace launched from a kitchen table - and today, over 10 million guests a year attend a Togather-powered event. Across every project, our mission remains the same:
  
  
To make events better for everyone.
  
  
**The Role:**
We're looking for a Content & Social Media Manager to deliver Togather's social and content from idea to reporting. This is a hands-on role: you'll shoot and edit video and photography at events, venues and with suppliers, and build a network of freelance photographers, videographers and creators to cover our growing calendar, including peak season. You'll work to our brand strategy with input from our Head of Brand, reporting directly into our CMO.
  
  
**Working pattern**
This isn't a desk-based 9 to 5. You'll split your time between our London office, home and our events, averaging two events or site visits a week, including evenings and weekends, with a heavier schedule through festival season and Christmas. Time off in lieu is agreed in advance.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Own content end to end: planning, production, publishing and review, across all our event types
* Keep a rolling three-month content calendar and seasonal peak plans, with briefs out three weeks before every event
* Shoot and edit video and photography at events, venues and with suppliers
* Source, brief and manage freelance photographers, videographers and creators, within budget
* Run our Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok and content hub, keeping a consistent cadence and engaging our community

* Keep our live, sales and leadership teams involved, and build relationships with event leads and partners

**Requirements**

* 4+ years in social and content, with at least two owning channel strategy and growth for a brand

* Experience planning content months ahead

* Confident with social analytics and reporting
* Happy to work evenings and weekends on site, especially in peak season

* Experience in live events, hospitality, food and drink, or B2B and B2C marketplaces
* Professional camera kit experience, plus Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, Lightroom and CapCut
* Experience running creator or user-generated content programmes, or employee advocacy on LinkedIn

* Partnership with Benefits Platform Mintago; EAP service, Workplace Nursery, Cycle to work scheme, Electric car scheme, Health services, Mental Health services, Gym discounts, retail discounts and much more
* Partnership with Code app: Significant discounts in a lot of London's best restaurants, bars and more

### **About the role**

**Tl;DR- Can you build internal relationships & tell external stories? ✨**

Blink is the universal AI platform for frontline work. We're building it because AI is the defining technology of our generation, yet thousands of frontline organisations risk being left behind because their workforce remains disconnected from the rest of the business.

We have a framework for our differentiation and the stories we want to tell. What we're missing is the person with the lateral thinking and end-to-end discipline to actually find, source, and create the customer evidence that makes those stories real - data and anecdotes, not just claims.

This is a founding mandate: build that discipline from scratch, and make it the engine behind three things at once - the website, our AI positioning, and how we tell customer stories at all.

### **What you'll own**

* Find the stories nobody’s told yet. You will be digging across our customers, and the CS, implementation, and sales teams who know them, for the moments that show our real value.
* Put a number on every story. We’re building a credible and quality brand, the real stories have proof behind them. Faster onboarding, lower churn, hours saved. No anecdote ships without impact data behind it.
* Make the website the gospel. You will be a core part of ensuring our killer web pages perform. Pages that are backed with credible stories, data and proof no generic claims here!
* Turn one story into ten. Be the expert in slicing and dicing. Every story feeds multiple sources. The newsletter, our blog, SEO, events, and sales enablement.
* Own our advocates. Manage our amazing customers who go on record for us, as a peer to their VPs and C-suite.
* Run the tight ship. This is about rigor and process to ensure a smooth marketing engine. You’ll be owning the quarterly content plan and publishing schedule end to end, and use AI to ship at the pace of a small team.

 **Requirements**  

### **What you'll bring**

* Experience in a customer marketing or advocacy function at a fast scaling B2B SaaS company - this needs someone who has built from very little before, not someone doing it for the first time.
* A researcher's instinct - comfortable digging for the anecdote and the number behind it rather than waiting to be handed both.
* Comfort managing relationships with VP and C-suite customer contacts as equals.
* Strong writing instincts and a good ear for our voice - human and substantive, never fluffy or immature.
* Judgment about what to prioritise first when the mandate is broad and nothing exists yet.

### **First 90 days look like**

* A repeatable method exists for finding and sourcing customer stories - not a one-off case study, a process.
* At least one flagship customer relationship has produced a story with real data attached, in a new format.
* A clear definition of what "great" looks like for a Blink video case study or EGC piece, even if production capacity to scale it doesn't exist yet.

  
**Benefits**  

### **Why Blink?**

You’ll have the opportunity to be part of something impactful, large-scale, and meaningful. Most importantly, you’ll be working in a company with a strong mission and with a team that is ambitious and embarking on a journey that many start-ups can only dream of!

**Other benefits include:**

* Competitive salary.
* Stock options on starting and additional high performer grants annually!
* 25 days’ leave + public holidays.
* Additional time off between Christmas and New Year.
* Private healthcare with AXA.
* 3% employer pension contribution when you contribute 5%.
* Cycle to Work scheme.
* Social events ( lunches, breakfasts, nights out).
* Enhanced parental leave.

Customers in a diverse range of industries, with particular growth in wealth management, financial services and supply chain onboarding.

Demand accelerating beyond our UK headquarters, across multiple continents with new customers in the Middle East, Asia, and Oceania.

This isn’t just another job role; it’s an opportunity to shape the future of the due diligence industry with a market-leading product trusted by global organisations. Whether you’re in marketing, communications, sales, or finance, you’ll play a critical role in driving growth, building credibility, and defining how we connect our product to a rapidly evolving market.

For people who love learning, innovating, and making an impact that matters now is the moment to be a part of Xapien.

**About the role**

As Campaign Manager, you'll own the planning and delivery of Xapien's integrated marketing campaigns, turning our story into pipeline. You'll run multi-channel digital programmes, ensure our events, conferences and webinars generate revenue.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves both the creative and the analytical side of marketing: you'll write the brief, build the workflows, get the audience in the room, and report on what it delivered. You’ll work extremely closely with our Sales team as part of one “demand generation” center of excellence to ensure not only that we get to the right people with the right message at the right time, but those leads get perfectly timed seamless engagement from other team members.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape our campaigns functions as a founding member, with more colleagues to join you in the new year.

**Campaign planning and execution**

* Plan, build and run end-to-end, results-driven campaigns across email, paid, social, content and events, from brief through to launch and optimisation
* Own campaign set-up in HubSpot (or similar marketing automation platforms): segmented lists, email nurtures, workflows, landing pages, forms and lead scoring
* Set clear goals and KPIs for every campaign (MQLs, SQLs, pipeline, conversion rates) and track performance against them
* Analyse results, run A/B tests and use the insights to continuously improve targeting, content and conversion
* Maintain a campaign calendar and coordinate timelines with Product Marketing, Content, Design and Sales
* Keep CRM and campaign data clean and accurate, and ensure accurate attribution and reporting

**Events, conferences and webinars**

* Plan and manage Xapien's presence at industry events and conferences, including booth logistics, supplier management, shipping, collateral and on-site coordination
* Run our webinar programme end to end: topic and speaker sourcing, platform set-up, rehearsals, promotion and post-event follow-up
* Build pre-event promotion and post-event nurture campaigns to drive registrations, attendance and meetings booked
* Manage event budgets and measure ROI, including pipeline influenced and sourced

The Marketing Operations Manager owns the top of Marcura's funnel: how leads and target accounts arrive, how they are enriched, scored and routed, and how we prove which marketing activity creates pipeline and revenue.

2 deliverables define the first 6 months: a trusted top of funnel process from lead to opportunity, and a multi touch attribution model that sales, marketing and leadership rely on. * Recycle and nurture leads that are not yet ready for sales, so none are lost.
* Own lead volume, quality and conversion targets, and run regular funnel reviews with sales leadership.

Headquartered in San Francisco, we’ve raised $277 million from investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, First Round, General Catalyst, and Elad Gil, most recently a $150 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation.
  
  
We’re building a team that moves quickly, takes ownership, and wants to make a meaningful impact on how the world’s largest organizations work. Come help us build what’s next for enterprise service management.
  
  
**Role Overview**
The opportunities that matter most are often the hardest to get in front of. As our first Field Marketing & ABM hire in EMEA, you'll partner directly with Sales to build our field motion in the region from zero: high-impact programs across segments and 1:1 ABM plays for our most strategic accounts. You'll challenge the status quo in field marketing to create unique experiences and moments that open doors, build trust, and move deals forward.

**Who You Are**

* Creative and opportunistic. You see an opening where others see a closed door. You know that breaking through to hard-to-reach accounts isn't about budget, it's about timing, creativity, and understanding what matters.
* Allergic to "best practices" that produce mediocre results. You'd rather test something bold than execute something safe.
* A doer, not a delegator. You're equally comfortable building a Salesforce report, negotiating with a venue in Shoreditch, or sending a llama with an invite around its neck to a CIO's office in Canary Wharf.

* Define the EMEA go-to-market strategy for field programs: what we do, where we show up, and how we win across UK&I, DACH, Benelux, and the Nordics.

**What You'll Need**

Compensation Range: £110K - £150K

Ministry of Sound opened in 1991 in a disused bus garage in a forgotten corner of South London. It was the first nightclub in the UK to have a 24-hour licence, didn’t serve alcohol and featured an earth-shaking sound system in a specially constructed dance box.

We went on to become the world’s largest independent record company, now with Sony, and stage giant dance events. We were pioneers in electronic music and have a history of taking risks, innovation, and colourful and creative marketing.

Thirty years later we opened The Ministry, a workspace run as a member’s club, in a 50,000 sq. ft Victorian warehouse in SE1. The design is relaxed but functional with a bar, opening windows, an outside courtyard and plenty of space to sit, relax, work and socialise – everything you wouldn’t expect to find in a standard office. There’s great home cooked F&B, a state-of-the-art gym and fitness studio with daily classes, together with a cultural and business events programme.

Also, Ministry of Sound Games is an ambitious new global venture at the intersection of mass participation fitness, music and entertainment. Building on the cultural impact of Ministry of Sound, our mission is to deliver world-class, high-energy fitness events and experiences that redefine how people connect through movement, music and competition.

As a business we don’t take ourselves too seriously, like to laugh and have fun, but we have high standards, a relentless attention to detail and the continuous improvement of our product, and we work hard as a team. We hate cliché, doing things the way others do and continuously seek to differentiate our brands and products almost as a point of pride.

**THE ROLE**

We want a membership marketer who has built a community brand from the inside, not run one from a head office. You'll own how The Ministry grows, from the first post someone sees to their tour, their first month and the friend they refer a year later.

It's a small team: you, our Content & Social Producer and Marketing Executive. You'll set the plan, and you'll also write the newsletter, brief the shoot, tweak the ads and host the members' event.

You're probably the marketing lead, or the number two, at a boutique fitness or wellness brand, a design-led workspace or members' club, or a lifestyle, events or culture brand with a membership model. If you're used to a large in-house team, a big agency roster and a specialist for every channel, this probably isn't the role for you. If you want more ownership, a bigger brand behind you and a clear line from your work to revenue, it is.
